newsitem.title: UK: Prudential shares slip after in-line results.
newsitem.headline: Prudential shares slip after in-line results.

text.p: Shares in Prudential Corp Plc fell slightly at the open, amid doubts over its acquisition strategy after reporting first-half profits that matched expectations, traders said.
At 0740 GMT, Pru shares dipped 1p to 609, against a stronger FTSE 100 open.
"The impression from the market is that it was a good set of numbers but the shares have already had a bit of bounce...so it could be hard to justify much further gains right now," one trader said.
"There are a few doubts about strategy in terms of acquiring someone else," he said.
Prudential, Britain's largest life insurance company, said pre-tax operating profits rose to 442 million sterling from 421 million a year ago.
Excluding income from disposals made in 1996, profits from continuing operations were up 19 percent over the period.
The Pru increased the dividend by 10.3 percent to 6.4 pence per share, which, following the changes made in the July budget, is to be paid as a foreign income dividend.
In the UK, the company said its main objectives were to continue to expand its product range and distribution capabilities and building its customer base.
On Tuesday, Prudential's shares rose to a high of 615p, off a low of 553p touched on July 21.
